clue.text: Love couple shown round ruined castle — it presents various challenges (12, two words)

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: one piece is shown going round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds

indicators.note: something ruined is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of lovers tour a ruined castle, which tests them in different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' and 'couple' paint a romance, but they are zero and a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle race is a race over a course of hurdles, nets, walls and other obstacles to overcome.

clue.text: One left phone off before service — it produces high blasts

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: off means faulty or out of order, so the letters are disarranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
the Royal Navy is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone turns off their phone before a church service, and then the trumpets sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests worship, but it is one of the armed forces. 'High' means up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpenhorn is a very long wooden horn blown by herdsmen in the Alps, so its blasts sound at altitude.

clue.text: Wager rarely about speed where rockets are launched

indicators.note: one word goes about another, wrapping round it on both sides

parts.note: Chambers gives 'to wager' as a rare sense of sport, hence 'rarely'
rate of movement

explanation.surface: A gambler occasionally bets on how fast something will go, perhaps a racing driver or a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' is not frequency here but a dictionary label: wagering is a rare sense of the verb sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceport is a base built for launching and receiving spacecraft, a launch site for rockets.

clue.text: Like toffs in fur, open to prosecution

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: sable is the fur of a small Arctic mammal
U means upper-class, the way toffs (posh people) speak and behave

explanation.surface: Posh people in furs could find themselves facing a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class usage, as against non-U; a toff is an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Suable means capable of being sued, so liable to legal action.

clue.text: Endlessly soft around evening, like river in idyllic setting

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the next one, enclosing it
without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for soft
ene is an old poetic form of even, meaning evening

explanation.surface: Endless gentle murmuring around evening, like a stream in a pastoral scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is the Peneus in Thessaly, flowing through the vale of Tempe, the classic idyllic landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Peneian is the adjective for the river Peneus, which waters Tempe, the vale poets made a byword for rural bliss.

clue.text: Pumpkin when brought in to munch US-style

indicators.note: a word brought in is taken inside another

parts.note: chaw is dialect and American for chew
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: An American pumpkin is fetched in to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashaw, also spelt cushaw, is an American crookneck squash or pumpkin.

clue.text: Some chap's stentorian, attention-seeking utterance

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters are used

parts.note: letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A man's booming cry trying to get noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Stentorian means very loud, the opposite of the quiet sound defined, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissed sound made to catch someone's attention quietly.

clue.text: Blokes from Cape Town in French town run off south

indicators.note: the named letter goes off, leaving the town's name without it

parts.note: Rouen is a city in Normandy
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Some men from Cape Town flee a French town, heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: Ou is South African slang for a man or bloke; Chambers gives this plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouens is the plural of ou, a South African colloquial word for a man, a chap or bloke.

clue.text: Oldie's stiff collar and jaunty boater

indicators.note: jaunty means set at a rakish angle, so the letters are tilted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old gentleman's outfit: a starched collar and a straw hat worn at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat. 'Oldie's' means the word itself is old-fashioned, not that the wearer is.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebato was a stiff, wired collar standing up behind the head, worn in the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: E.g. mistletoe, making naughty pastime arise

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so the letters refuse to stay in order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Mistletoe gets kissing going, a naughty Christmas pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to kissing under the mistletoe; the plant is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is a semiparasite: it makes its own food by photosynthesis but draws water and minerals from its host tree.

clue.text: Old Scot? A clue to be solved in birthplace

indicators.note: the reworked letters are placed inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: standard abbreviation for birthplace

indicators.note: a clue to be solved must be worked out, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about an elderly Scotsman, solved by looking at where he was born.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: Scots were nicknamed for their blue bonnets.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluecap is an old nickname for a Scotsman, after the blue woollen bonnet traditionally worn in Scotland.

clue.text: Dad's trapped this seal

indicators.note: the first word has trapped the other inside itself

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father; the 's is 'has'
hoc is Latin for this, as in ad hoc

explanation.surface: Father has caught this seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' looks like a pointer to the seal, but it is a Latin word to translate.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoca is the genus of the common seal, and Chambers lists it as a word for a seal.

clue.text: Petitioned for termination of crocodile leather

parts.note: to sue for something is to petition for it, as in sued for peace

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone went to court to end the trade in crocodile skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Crocodile leather is a red herring: the leather defined is the napped calfskin kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather, usually kid or calf, with its flesh side rubbed into a soft velvety nap.

clue.text: Barking shins, dad restrained language

indicators.note: the reworked letters hold the next word in, as a restraint would
barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A child barks his shins and his father keeps his language in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking shins' reads as scraping the legs, but barking is British slang for crazy and signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish is the Romance language of Spain and much of Latin America.

clue.text: Fatty stuff: whole amount has sink almost stuffed

indicators.note: something stuffed has another thing packed inside it

parts.note: a sum is a total, the whole amount

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to ebb is to sink or decline

explanation.surface: A kitchen note: a greasy residue has clogged the whole sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like the kitchen basin, but it is a verb meaning decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebum is the oily secretion of the skin's sebaceous glands, a fatty substance.

clue.text: About now in Israel, note, Bethlehem holds this

indicators.note: the run of letters holds the target within it, spanning the word break

parts.note: letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A seasonal remark about Bethlehem near Christmas, a note on what it holds now.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in early December, which falls in this Hebrew month; hence 'About now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tebeth is the tenth month of the Jewish calendar, roughly December to January, the current month in Israel at publication.

clue.text: Alien

parts.note: the bare definition of the competition word
in a plain competition puzzle solvers write this clue themselves, so only a definition is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was the competition word: Azed gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a person from another country, a native of somewhere else, which is what this noun names.

clue.text: Rounders fielder supports spinner

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a spinning top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A rounders team's fielder backs up the bowler who spins the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game like baseball. 'Spinner' suggests a bowler, but it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: In rounders, as in baseball, the backstop is the fielder positioned behind the batter, like a catcher.

clue.text: Cold, then high temperature? It's deceptive

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the answer is a noun, a thing that deceives

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
heat is high temperature

explanation.surface: A shivering patient then has a fever, a misleading set of symptoms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat can be a noun for a fraud or deception, something that misleads.

clue.text: Demand from appreciative audience welcomed by musician (cor anglais)

indicators.note: the target is welcomed into, sitting inside, the following words

parts.note: letters run from the end of the first word into the bracket

explanation.surface: A cor anglais player is welcomed by an audience calling for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancora is Italian for 'again', an audience's call for an encore.

clue.text: It's essential to indicate ransackers…or one of them?

indicators.note: what is essential to words lies at their core, inside them

parts.note: letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Pointing to looters is vital, or maybe pointing to one of the gang?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' refers back to the ransackers, so the answer is one of the raiders the words describe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cateran was a Highland marauder or freebooter, a raider who plundered and pillaged.

clue.text: Borrower, person alternating with ale drunk

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up
taking turns letter by letter, the two words are interwoven rather than joined end to end

parts.note: one is a person, as in 'one should'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A borrower who takes turns with the drinking of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, ALE jumbled to L-A-E has its letters alternated with O-N-E: L, O, A, N, E, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A loanee is the recipient of a loan, so a borrower.

clue.text: S. American people certainly got on top of local rodent

parts.note: ay is an old form of yes, certainly
the mara is a hare-like rodent native to Patagonia, local to South America

explanation.surface: South Americans definitely beat the rodent pests where they live.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the piece that is on top comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aymara are an indigenous people of the Andes in Bolivia and Peru, around Lake Titicaca.

clue.text: Boarding conceals king once shut in

indicators.note: what is concealed is hidden from view, so those letters disappear

parts.note: boarding a ship or plane is embarking on it
the very word printed, removed from the end

explanation.surface: A monarch going aboard hides himself away, once confined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Embar is an old verb meaning to shut in or enclose, as behind bars.

clue.text: Numbers ruined in absence of right conductors

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are thrown about
in the absence of a letter means without it, so it is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bungled set of figures with no correct answers, like an orchestra without its conductors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductors' suggests music or electricity, but here it means bus crews.
explanation.definitionFit: Bus conductors, who collected fares on buses, are among busmen, the men who work on buses.

clue.text: Dido, see, on a pyre lit with toyboy finally leaving?

indicators.note: lit means set alight, or drunk, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the named letter leaves the group, departing from it

parts.note: the letter C is said just like the word see
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, its closing letter

parts.note: the final letter, picked out by 'finally'

explanation.surface: Queen Dido mounts her blazing pyre as her young lover Aeneas sails away.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido looks like the tragic queen, but a dido is also a prank, and 'see' is the letter C by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dido is to play a prank, and a caper is likewise a frolic or mischievous trick.

clue.text: Guest paying to imbibe a strong drink, gauging extent?

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, taking something inside

parts.note: PG stands for paying guest, a lodger
a plus gin, a strong spirit

explanation.surface: A lodger pays for the strong spirits they drink, judging how much to take?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: numbering a book's pages measures how long it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Paging is numbering the pages of a book, which fixes and so shows its length.

clue.text: Reverse of old-fashioned on holding one crucifer

indicators.note: the reverse of something is read the other way round
the reversed letters hold another piece inside them

parts.note: mumsy means dowdy and old-fashioned
re means on or concerning
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone backward in style carries a single cross, like a church crucifer.
explanation.walkthrough: A crucifer is usually a cross-bearer in a procession, but botanically it is a plant of the cabbage family.
explanation.definitionFit: Erysimum, the treacle mustard and wallflower genus, belongs to the Cruciferae, plants with cross-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Shoddy, old, in places it is covered in rust, maltreated

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is enclosed by it
something maltreated is knocked about, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
Chambers gives a as a dialect word for it, used in some places

explanation.surface: Something shoddy and old, here and there covered in rust from rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In places' looks like 'here and there' but is a dialect label. 'Old' tags the definition as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Surat was a coarse cotton cloth from the Indian city of Surat, and so came to mean anything of inferior quality.

clue.text: Cross, but without anger or heat of old

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a saltire is an X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Angry but not angry, or hot under the collar in an old way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to mean angry, alongside 'anger', but it is the heraldic cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt is an obsolete word for sexual heat in a female animal, so heat in an old sense.

clue.text: Hide that's dropped in for clutch stabilizers?

indicators.note: the hide has dropped the word that follows, losing it

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
the very word printed, which the hide drops
a clutch is a nestful of eggs

explanation.surface: A hidden car clutch has dropped in, so in come the stabilizers?
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' in the clue is the letters removed, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skegs are fins on a surfboard or keel extensions on a boat that keep it stable; Chambers allows the double-g spelling.

clue.text: A physicist giving up day to identify source of exotic timber

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: giving something up means letting it go, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Michael Faraday, the English physicist
the very word printed, removed from the surname

explanation.surface: A scientist takes a day off to trace where some foreign wood came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Afara is a West African tree whose pale timber is exported, so a source of foreign wood.

clue.text: Westward travellers in Italy for putti

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left

parts.note: the Roma are the Romani people, often called travellers
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Tourists heading west through Italy in search of cherub paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travellers' suggests tourists, but here it means the Roma people.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorini and putti are both plurals for chubby winged cupid figures in Renaissance art.

clue.text: Teething aid, child's first relating to the mouth

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter
oral means of the mouth

explanation.surface: Something to help a teething child, which naturally goes in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies were traditionally given a piece of polished coral to chew on when cutting teeth.

clue.text: P.Cezanne's friend follows rules in postponed case

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for rule
Paul Cezanne's friend was the painter Edouard Manet, written with his initial

explanation.surface: A painter's friend sticks to the rules in a court case that was put off.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial P. for Paul is the hint: the friend is given the same style, E. MANET. 'Follows' puts him after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A remanet is a legal case or parliamentary bill held over to a later sitting, so a postponed case.

clue.text: Reassembled tent in bag requiring wooden support structure

indicators.note: reassembled means put together again in a new form

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A camper puts a tent back together, finding it in a bag needing wooden poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Battening is a structure of battens, thin strips of wood that support or strengthen.
